FAQ

Does shipping trackpad support auto-translate my China listing?

No. Pointer interaction, scroll recognition, and three-finger gesture handling are in-app features — they do not fill App Store Connect localization rows. If zh-Hans fields are empty, the China product page falls back to en-US copy.

How is this different from Magic Keyboard listing copy?

Magic Keyboard marketing covers the folio keyboard-and-trackpad cover as one accessory — physical keyboard typing, iPadOS shortcuts, 妙控键盘, 键盘快捷键. Trackpad marketing covers pointer navigation and gestures — cursor, click, scroll, secondary click, pinch zoom, three-finger gestures — 触控板, 妙控板, 指针, 双指滚动. Keyboard-and-keys vs trackpad pointer — different listing story.

How is this different from Apple Pencil Hover or Scribble?

Apple Pencil Hover covers pre-contact ink preview — 悬停预览. Scribble covers handwriting-to-text in text fields — 随手写. Trackpad marketing covers external pointer devices — Magic Keyboard trackpad, Magic Trackpad, Bluetooth trackpad — cursor, click, scroll, and multi-finger gestures. See the Hover listing guide and Scribble listing guide when stylus input is your hero, not 触控板 pointer workflows.

How is this different from Pointer Control listing copy?

Pointer Control covers system Accessibility settings for mouse and trackpad — tracking speed, scrolling speed, pointer size — 指针控制, 鼠标辅助功能. This page covers in-app trackpad productivity marketing — cursor, scroll, secondary click, pinch zoom, three-finger gestures — not Accessibility pointer settings copy.

How is this different from Stage Manager, Split View, or Slide Over?

Stage Manager, Split View, and Slide Over cover iPad multitasking windowing — 台前调度, 分屏, 侧拉. This page covers trackpad pointer and gesture workflows — not resize handles, window shelves, or Side by Side chrome.

Yes — when your English listing markets trackpad pointer, scroll, and gesture workflows on the Magic Keyboard trackpad surface. Keyboard typing and shortcut keys belong on the Magic Keyboard listing guide; pointer navigation and gestures belong here.
